newsitem.title: MEXICO: POLL-Femsa Q2 net per share seen lower.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Femsa Q2 net per share seen lower.

text.p: Analysts predicted beverage company Fomento Economico Mexicano SA de CV (Femsa) would post improved sales and operating earnings but lower net earnings per share for the second quarter.
A Reuters survey of three analysts gave an average sales prediction of 5.914 billion pesos for the second quarter, up 6.6 percent in real terms from the same quarter last year.

Operating earnings were seen up 13.8 percent in real year-on-year terms to 667 million pesos. The analysts saw a fall in net earnings per share to 0.48 pesos from a year-ago figure of 0.70 pesos (restated in line with inflation).
"The comparison (in net earnings) will probably be negative because financial items have been falling off in line with inflation," said Francisco Chavez, an analyst with Smith Barney in New York.
Chavez said strong sales by Femsa's Coca-Cola bottling subsidiary Coca-Cola FEMSA SA could boost operating earnings.
"Coca-Cola FEMSA's results will be the most outstanding feature. They tell us sales volumes in Mexico City have been strong and growing at more than 10 percent," he said.
For Jorge Gutierrez of Inverlat, Femsa's brewing division may post operating improvements due to price increases, but overall sales volumes will likely be weak for the same reason.
"I feel the 22 percent price hike at the end of March will undermine beer sales, although I think we continue to see improvements on the operating line," he said.

The market had already largely discounted strong operating earnings for the second quarter, Scott Wilkins of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said. Femsa B shares were trading at 49.25 pesos at midday dealing on July 9, or up 83 percent for the year to date.
